channel.title: Embodied AI Weekly | 1N Robotics
channel.description: Weekly briefings and technical analysis on embodied intelligence, data, robot learning, and deployment.

item.title: From BEVFormer to UniAD: a one-year route from Pi3X geometry to persistent navigation
item.description: What to transfer into Compass 1-style systems, which experiments must come first, and when a robotics team should continue, simplify, or stop

item.title: Compass 1: what a single camera, geometric labels, and usable memory solve in robot navigation
item.description: Inside Archon’s navigation model: DJI Action 4 capture, monocular reconstruction, structured memory, video-action generation, and the gap to autonomous deployment

item.title: From BEVFormer and UniAD to WorldEngine and SimScale: learning from the states that demonstrations miss
item.description: How spatial memory and planning-oriented learning led to interactive data engines, and which lessons transfer from autonomous driving to robotics

item.title: Anchor1, SONIC, and SuperMimic: precision, scale, and the cost of control
item.description: Why a humanoid that can track a backflip can still miss a stationary reach, and what three control systems change about that problem

item.title: Ropedia's next step: from human video to reusable robot worlds
item.description: Xperience 2, reconstruction, world models, and control: what the data can support, where the interfaces remain incomplete, and how industrial teams should measure value

item.title: Robot learning after pretraining | Embodied AI Weekly
item.description: AMP1, RoboScript, MR0 revisions, and NVIDIA's CoRL stack reveal where corrections and rehearsal improve robots—and where deployment costs remain unproven

item.title: Ropedia W0: the data factory behind cross-embodiment world prediction
item.description: How human video, robot logs, and corrected kinematics become Xp-Data—and what the prediction and policy results actually establish

item.title: Why agentic robotics is accelerating: NVIDIA's loops and TinyAstral's RSI
item.description: NVIDIA's navigation, manipulation, policy-research, and agentic WAM loops, compared with TinyAstral's harness RSI and compact-model distillation.

item.title: From HumanWAM to GR00T 2: world-action models, data, and deployment
item.description: Architectures, aligned human and UMI data, benchmark protocols, reinforcement learning, and deployment costs across HumanWAM and GR00T 2.

item.title: CoRL 2026 dexterous hands: what Sharpa helps us see
item.description: A CoRL 2026 dexterity analysis through Sharpa Wave, comparing learning routes, tactile feedback, real-robot protocols, generalization, and industrial value.

item.title: Apple HALO: how a humanoid learns to move through a home
item.description: HALO's modular synthetic data, rendering, and training pipeline, with an analysis of generative rendering as a substitute for observation rendering and physical simulation.

item.title: MuJoCo 4: The Industrial Value of Better Simulation
item.description: The industrial value of better contact simulation, collaboration, calibrated training, and measurable robot development costs.

item.title: NVIDIA GR00T 2: World-Action Models Meet Deployment Reality
item.description: A deployment-focused analysis of GR00T 2's world-action architecture, data, generalization, dexterity, agentic recovery, and onboard latency.

item.title: Did GPT-6 Astra Change the Robotics Roadmap?
item.description: A post-release evaluation of how GPT-6 Astra changes the division of labor among VLA, WAM, agentic systems, embodied in-context learning, and tactile control.

item.title: From Predicting the Next Frame to Orchestrating the Next Step: Agentic WAM, MoT, and Dexterous Control
item.description: An analysis of the three-expert MoT in NVIDIA-linked AW-0, compared with EgoScale, T-Rex, DexTacWAM, and Dexplore.

item.title: From Human Video to Robot Action: DA Group's HumanScale and HumanWAM Roadmap
item.description: How Open-HumanScale-50K, HumanWAM-Vanilla, and HumanWAM-Goal transfer egocentric human experience into robot action.

item.title: Tactile reaction, field reliability, and collaborative robot learning
item.description: Four developments that moved embodied AI closer to useful physical systems this week.
